FINDING | contract: Raffle | function: releaseSponsorProceeds | bug_class: premature-sponsor-payout | group_key: Raffle | releaseSponsorProceeds | premature-sponsor-payout
path: sponsor calls RaffleFactory.createRaffle(prizeToken, ...) -> buyers call Raffle.buyEntries(...) -> Raffle.requestDraw() and Raffle.fulfillRandomWords() set status = Status.NftWon -> sponsor calls Raffle.settleWinningTicket(winningTicketId) and Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds() -> winner calls Raffle.redeemWinningTicket(winningTicketId) -> prizeToken.transferFrom(address(this), winner, deliveredPrizeTokenId) reverts -> sponsor keeps 95% of USDC pot while winner cannot redeem NFT or call enableRefunds()
proof: In Raffle._settleWinningTicket (lines 536-561), when result == Status.NftWon, the contract sets sponsorProceeds = grossPot - protocolFee (95% of unsettledPot) without transferring prizeToken. In Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds (lines 378-385), the contract transfers sponsorProceeds to sponsorRecipient without checking prizeClaimed or winnerRedeemed. RaffleFactory.createRaffle (lines 777-802) accepts any contract that returns true for supportsInterface(type(IERC721).interfaceId). If a sponsor creates a raffle with reserveEntries = 100 using an ERC-721 contract that blocks transfers after escrow (or a pausable/controllable ERC-721 that gets paused), and buyers purchase 100 entries for 100,000,000 raw USDC (100 USDC), VRF resolution sets status = Status.NftWon. The sponsor calls settleWinningTicket and releaseSponsorProceeds to withdraw 95,000,000 raw USDC (95 USDC). When the winner calls redeemWinningTicket, prizeToken.transferFrom reverts (line 337), and enableRefunds reverts with InvalidStatus(Status.NftWon) (line 296), so the winner loses 100 USDC and receives no prize while the sponsor profits 95 USDC.
description: A sponsor whose prizeToken blocks transfers after escrow can call releaseSponsorProceeds to take 95% of the pot while redeemWinningTicket fails.
fix: Transfer prizeToken to the owner of the ticket inside _settleWinningTicket, or require prizeClaimed to be true when status is Status.NftWon in releaseSponsorProceeds.

FINDING | contract: Raffle | function: buyEntries | bug_class: sponsor-rebate-ticket-dilution | group_key: Raffle | buyEntries | sponsor-rebate-ticket-dilution
path: buyers call Raffle.buyEntries(...) -> sponsor calls Raffle.buyEntries(sponsor, entryCount) right before endTime -> Raffle.requestDraw() and Raffle.fulfillRandomWords() set status = Status.NftWon -> sponsor calls Raffle.settleWinningTicket(winningTicketId) and Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds() -> sponsor recovers 95% of own entry payment while capturing majority odds to win back prizeToken or force Status.NftWon
proof: In Raffle.buyEntries (lines 212-240), there is no cap on totalEntries (except type(uint128).max) and no restriction on sponsor purchasing entries. In Raffle._settleWinningTicket (lines 543-547), when status == Status.NftWon, sponsorProceeds = grossPot - protocolFee = 95% of unsettledPot. Therefore, every 1,000,000 raw USDC (1 USDC) the sponsor spends on buyEntries returns 950,000 raw USDC (0.95 USDC) to sponsorRecipient via sponsorProceeds, for a net cost of only 50,000 raw USDC (0.05 USDC, the 5% protocol fee) per entry versus 1.00 USDC for honest buyers. Concrete trace 1 (post-reserve dilution): Prize NFT value = 10,000 USDC, reserveEntries = 10,000. Honest buyers buy 10,000 entries (10,000 USDC). At endTime - 1, the sponsor calls buyEntries(sponsor, 90,000) for 90,000 USDC. Upon settlement, the sponsor receives 95% of 100,000 USDC = 95,000 USDC via releaseSponsorProceeds (net cash +5,000 USDC) and holds 90,000 / 100,000 = 90% probability of winning back the 10,000 USDC NFT (9,000 USDC expected value, total expected value 14,000 USDC), reducing honest buyers' win probability from 100% to 10%. Concrete trace 2 (reserve-crossing): reserveEntries = 1,000, NFT value = 100 USDC, honest buyers buy 600 entries (600 USDC). Instead of accepting Status.CashWon (15% sponsor share = 90 USDC + 100 USDC NFT = 190 USDC), the sponsor buys 400 entries (400 USDC) at endTime - 1 to reach reserveEntries = 1,000 (Status.NftWon), collects 950 USDC via releaseSponsorProceeds (550 USDC net cash) plus a 40% chance at the 100 USDC NFT (590 USDC total expected value, extracting +400 USDC from buyers).
description: A sponsor can call buyEntries and recover 95% of that payment through releaseSponsorProceeds, so the sponsor dilutes other buyers for a 5% fee.
fix: Cap totalEntries at reserveEntries or a fixed maximum entry count in buyEntries, and reject purchases from sponsor and sponsorRecipient.

FINDING | contract: RaffleFactory | function: createRaffle | bug_class: unbounded-reserve-entries | group_key: RaffleFactory | createRaffle | unbounded-reserve-entries
path: sponsor calls RaffleFactory.createRaffle with unreachable reserveEntries -> victim calls Raffle.buyEntries(...) -> at endTime, sponsor calls Raffle.requestDraw() -> Raffle.fulfillRandomWords() sets status = Status.CashWon because totalEntries < reserveEntries -> sponsor calls Raffle.settleWinningTicket, Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds, and Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize -> sponsor recovers prizeToken and takes 15% of victim USDC deposits
proof: RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams (line 801) only checks if (params.reserveEntries == 0) revert ZeroReserveEntries() with no upper bound on uint128 reserveEntries, and Raffle.requestDraw (lines 243-250) allows any caller (including sponsor) to trigger a draw whenever totalEntries >= 1, even when totalEntries < reserveEntries. When totalEntries < reserveEntries, Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (line 524) sets status = Status.CashWon, and Raffle._settleWinningTicket (lines 548-551) allocates 80% (CASH_WINNER_BPS = 8000) to winnerProceeds, 5% (PROTOCOL_FEE_BPS = 500) to protocolFees, and 15% (1500 bps) to sponsorProceeds, while Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize (lines 398-410) returns prizeToken to sponsorRecipient. Concrete trace: Sponsor sets reserveEntries = type(uint128).max (or 1,000,000) and a buyer purchases 50 entries for 50,000,000 raw USDC (50 USDC). Even though no other buyer participates and the reserve is missed, the buyer cannot claim a refund at endTime; the sponsor calls requestDraw(), recovers the NFT via releaseSponsorPrize(), and withdraws 15% = 7,500,000 raw USDC (7.50 USDC) via releaseSponsorProceeds(), while the sole buyer loses 10,000,000 raw USDC (10 USDC, 20% of deposit).
description: A sponsor can set an unreachable reserveEntries and call requestDraw after endTime, so the sponsor keeps the prize and takes 15% of deposits.
fix: Enforce a reasonable upper bound on reserveEntries in _validateCreateParams, or route raffles that miss reserveEntries to Status.Refunding instead of Status.CashWon.

FINDING | contract: Raffle | function: enableRefunds | bug_class: cancellation-frontrun-lock | group_key: Raffle | enableRefunds | cancellation-frontrun-lock
path: sponsor calls Raffle.enableRefunds() on an empty raffle before endTime -> attacker front-runs with Raffle.buyEntries(attacker, 1) for 1 USDC -> totalEntries becomes 1 -> sponsor's Raffle.enableRefunds() reverts with RefundsNotAvailable(drawRequestDeadline(), block.timestamp) -> sponsor's prizeToken is locked until endTime or drawRequestDeadline()
proof: In Raffle.enableRefunds (lines 282-291), when status == Status.Active, pre-endTime cancellation by sponsor is only allowed if totalEntries == 0; if totalEntries > 0, enableRefunds reverts with RefundsNotAvailable(drawRequestDeadline(), block.timestamp) until endTime + 2 days. Concrete trace: Sponsor creates a raffle with endTime = block.timestamp + 30 days (MAX_SALE_DURATION) and submits enableRefunds() while totalEntries == 0 to cancel and recover prizeToken. An attacker front-runs with buyEntries(attacker, 1) costing 1,000,000 raw USDC (1.00 USDC). The sponsor's enableRefunds() call reverts, locking prizeToken for up to 30 days (if the sponsor pays the VRF fee in requestDraw() at endTime, where the attacker still recovers 800,000 raw USDC = 0.80 USDC via redeemWinningTicket for a net attack cost of 0.20 USDC, or wins prizeToken outright if reserveEntries == 1) or 32 days (if no draw is requested, where the attacker recovers all 1,000,000 raw USDC = 1.00 USDC via refundTickets for a net attack cost of 0 USDC).
description: An attacker can call buyEntries with one entry before a sponsor calls enableRefunds, which blocks cancellation and locks prizeToken until endTime for one USDC.
fix: Add a startTime delay before buyEntries accepts purchases so the sponsor can call enableRefunds during a grace period after creation.

code_smells: sponsorRecipient and protocolTreasury are immutable and lack a fallback address when quoteToken blacklists them.
description: The quoteToken issuer can blacklist the immutable sponsorRecipient or protocolTreasury and lock those payouts forever, though this requires an external action by Circle.
